summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 4 upside misses — LR.PA +2%, III.L +2%, ANTO.L +2%, BESI.AS +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (BMW.DE -7%, ORA.PA -3%, VOW3.DE -2%, ENT.L -2%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: BMW.DE (-7.28%) — BMW issued a profit warning (released Jun 16 after-hours) cutting 2026 automotive EBIT margin guidance to 1–3% from 4–6%, citing an accelerating China sales slump and Iran war-driven demand/cost headwinds. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — BMW.DE is a DAX large-cap automaker not in current coverage. The warning dropped Jun 16 post-close; only pre-open short positioning before Frankfurt open could have captured the gap, leaving reactive intraday filters with no viable entry.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector sympathy move: Bernstein's June 15 Outperform reiteration on ASML (€1,700 PT) citing semiconductor equipment pricing power recovery rippled to EU equipment peers; no ASM-specific news found for June 17.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ASM.AS (~€50B cap, €1,017/share) is likely excluded by a per-share price or lot-size filter; the move was also sector-driven (ASML contagion), leaving no idiosyncratic signal available to trigger entry before the gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Wire macro-aligned's sector-momentum gate to ASML: when ASML gains >1.5% on a broker-note day, allow long entry in correlated EU equipment peers (ASM.AS, Aixtron) within 90 min of Amsterdam open, subject to existing risk limits.

top_movers.catalyst: Musk made a virtual appearance at ASML's annual tech conference unveiling Terafab — a $55B SpaceX/Tesla/xAI chip initiative requiring ASML's exclusive EUV systems — coinciding with SpaceX IPO pricing the same day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASML.AS is a ~€175B mega-cap on Euronext Amsterdam likely excluded by market-cap or exchange filters. The move was event-driven (CEO/partner conference reveal) requiring pre-market positioning before intraday signals could form.
top_movers.suggestion: Add ASML.AS to macro-aligned-hmm's EU large-cap watchlist as an AI-capex proxy; trigger a 0.5× sized entry when a verified conference/partnership catalyst appears in the pre-market news feed with gap ≥+1.5%.

top_movers.catalyst: Legrand's Jun 10 acquisition of Girtz Industries (~$80M rev, Power Pod datacenter specialist) — its 4th datacenter bolt-on in 2026 — continued to be priced in, reinforced by AI-infrastructure sector tailwinds across European industrials.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LR.PA is a CAC 40 large-cap French industrial (≈€15B mkt cap, electrical/digital building infra) uncovered by current geographic or sector filters. The move was M&A-momentum-driven, favouring pre-announcement positioning over post-open signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend the news-reactive strategy's universe to include CAC 40 electrical-infrastructure names (SIC-equivalent: digital/power building infra); trigger on acquisition press releases where target revenue ≥$50M and datacenter keyword present within 5 trading days of the release.

top_movers.catalyst: Last-day dividend capture before 48p (£0.48) second interim dividend goes ex on 2026-06-18; buying to qualify for the ~2% single-payment yield drove the day's +2.15% close-to-close move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — III.L is a FTSE 100 private-equity investment trust (3i Group), not a typical momentum or mean-reversion candidate. Move was mechanical pre-ex dividend-capture flow, not a scrapeable news catalyst; a news-reactive bot had no pre-market signal to act on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dividend-capture overnight scan: flag FTSE-universe names where ex-date = T+1 and the pending dividend payment ≥1.5% of prior close; enter a same-session long before the 4:30pm close and hard-exit at market open on ex-date to capture the pre-ex drift.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news identified; ANTO.L tracked LME copper (+0.35% to ~$6.51/lb on 17 Jun) as a high-beta pure-play copper miner — sector tailwind continuation from strong prior-week commodity rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ANTO.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap materials name (~£10B+ cap) whose price action is driven by LME copper spot rather than technical momentum signals; a commodity-equity beta sleeve is absent from the bot's strategy set.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a commodity-equity beta sleeve: enter FTSE 100 mining names (ANTO.L, GLEN.L, AAL.L) when LME 3-month copper closes ≥+0.4% on the prior session, with position sizing capped at 0.5% NAV per name to contain commodity concentration risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Pre-positioning ahead of BESI Investor Day (June 18, 1pm CET live webcast); underpinned by Q1 2026 beat — revenue +28.3% YoY, orders +104.5% YoY, Q2 guidance +30–40% sequential growth.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BESI is an Amsterdam-listed (AEX) large-cap (~€23bn) semiconductor equipment name trading at ~149× P/E — too high-multiple for value screens, and the pre-Investor Day drift is a low-volatility, calendar-anticipatory move that post-open momentum signals don't capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a T-1 calendar-event flag: AEX/Euronext large-cap names with a confirmed Investor Day or Capital Markets Day the next session AND trailing order growth >50% YoY should enter the news-reactive watchlist at open with a reduced size cap.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BMW.DE is a DAX large-cap automaker not in current coverage. The warning dropped Jun 16 post-close; only pre-open short positioning before Frankfurt open could have captured the gap, leaving reactive intraday filters with no viable entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a DAX/Euro-Stoxx large-cap earnings-gate: monitor official IR press releases for automotive EBIT-guidance cuts ≥2pp and emit a short-side signal if the pre-market indicated gap is ≥-4% within 15 min of Frankfurt open (09:15 CET).

top_movers.catalyst: Continued deal-digestion selling from the June 6 SFR/Altice France MOU — Orange committed ~€4.3B to absorb 4.9M SFR customers amid 4→3 antitrust uncertainty — while the broader CAC 40 rose +0.3%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ORA is a mega-cap French telecom (~€44B) held in income portfolios, not momentum screens. The -2.71% is multi-day post-MOU drift — a slow-burn that intraday gap/momentum filters are not designed to capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-MOU/M&A gate: any name in the active universe with a deal press release in the prior 14 days is blocked from new long entries until price reclaims its 5-day pre-announcement close.

top_movers.catalyst: BMW cut its FY2026 profit outlook citing China sales collapse and Iran-war energy cost spikes, sending BMW -7% and dragging the European auto sector down; pre-AGM jitters (Blume to confirm 19,000 job cuts on 18 Jun) compounded VOW3.DE's slide.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — VOW3.DE is a XETRA-listed European large-cap with no US ADR in scope. The move was peer-contagion driven (BMW warning) requiring cross-sector awareness, and the EUR 5.26 dividend ex-date on 19 Jun two days out would have distorted momentum/RSI signals even if the name were in-un
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sector-contagion short trigger: when a DAX auto-sector peer (BMW.DE, MBG.DE) drops ≥5% intraday, scan same-sector XETRA names for short entry within 30 min of open — gated on short capability being enabled; otherwise log as '(no actionable change — requires short and XETRA universe expansion)'.

top_movers.catalyst: UK Remote Gaming Duty hike (21%→40% from Apr 2026) continues to weigh on sector; Royal Ascot Day 2 bookmaker liability risk and negative PR from Entain/Ladbrokes dropping charity support compounded the move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Entain is an FTSE 100 UK gambling large-cap in structural decline (~30% YTD 2026). Long-only momentum strategies exclude downtrending names; a -2.11% decline requires short capability to capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE leisure/gambling names to a short-eligible universe triggered by confirmed RGD or equivalent tax-rate catalyst; gate entry on ≥3 consecutive sessions of sector underperformance vs FTSE 100 to avoid noise.
